scopeMarkdown:
Make `rayx-signalr` an independently versioned library that is released by **git tag**. Conventional Commits on `master` drive release-plz, which keeps a release pull request open and, when the owner merges it, tags `vX.Y.Z` and creates the GitHub Release. Nothing is published to a registry. The first release is **v1.0.0**, tagged by release-plz's `release` job on the one push that brings version `1.0.0` and the release workflow to `master`. Consumers (RayX first, in its own epic) then pin `rayx-signalr = { git = "https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.SignalR", tag = "vX.Y.Z" }`.

This epic follows the shared library-release template of 2026-10-18 (pilot: RayX.Dtcg `dtcg-releases`; model: RayX.CLI's release-plz setup without cargo-dist).

## In scope

- **release-plz configuration** (`release-plz.toml`): git-only, no registry, tag `v{{ version }}`, release-plz creates the GitHub Release, changelog from the CLI's template, `release_commits = "^(feat|fix|perf)"`, `semver_check = false` and `pr_branch_prefix = "release-plz-"`.
- **The 1.x policy** (owner, amendment 1): no repository leaves 1.x while the owner is the only consumer. No commit is marked breaking (no `!`, no `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer); a breaking change is a `feat` (or a `fix` when it is one) whose body states the break, with consumer notes in a `Migration:` footer that the changelog renders, so it bumps the minor. Before a release PR is merged its proposed version must still be `1.x`; a `2.0.0` proposal means a stray `!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:` commit, which is reworded (force push allowed) instead of merging. The policy ends when a second consumer appears.
- **Release workflow** (`.github/workflows/release-plz.yml`): the CLI's two jobs (`release`, `release-pr`) on pushes to `master` and `workflow_dispatch`, with the `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` PAT, Rust only, no tests.
- **Light CI on `master`** (owner, amendment 1 and its follow-up): `quality.yml` also runs on pushes to `master` (its pull-request trigger stays), but a push runs only the cheap ubuntu Rust jobs (rustfmt, clippy and the Rust unit tests); the Windows/macOS matrices, WASM, mobile, platform, rustdoc, dependency-security and contract jobs stay on pull requests. `e2e.yml` and `perf.yml` never run on push.
- **Repository governance**: the .NET `WorkflowContract` category accepts the fourth workflow and the Quality push trigger with narrow rules; new release contract groups (`Case=release-automation`, `Case=release-consumption`) prove the configuration, the workflow, the triggers, the release-PR guards, the version/changelog invariant and the tag-form install snippets.
- **Release-PR CI**: a release pull request (head `release-plz-*`) starts only `quality / rustfmt` and `quality / clippy`; every other Quality job and every End-to-end job is skipped by a job-level guard.
- **Version 1.0.0** in `Cargo.toml` and a new root `CHANGELOG.md` with a short hand-written `## [1.0.0] - <date>` section (what the client offers; no fabricated history).
- **Docs**: `docs/releasing.md`; the README `## Installation` section, `docs/01-getting-started.md`, `docs/08-tls.md` and the skill's install snippets in tag form; `docs/14-testing.md` CI section; `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` Releases section, Repository Layout and Consumers.
- **GitHub-dependent final sprint**: verify the existing `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` secret and `Release tags` ruleset, make the single (pre-approved) push, confirm the release-plz run that tags `v1.0.0` and creates the GitHub Release and the green light-Quality run of that push, and resolve the tag from a scratch consumer outside the repository.

## Out of scope

- crates.io or any registry (`publish = false` stays), and package `include`/`exclude` changes.
- RayX's switch to the tag (RayX epic `rayx-released-libraries`); RayX.GameX, which depends on this crate by path and checks this repository out in its CI (unaffected by the version bump; not changed here).
- Library source, API, tests or toolchain pins (the User-Agent follows the version automatically).
- Renovate, Dependabot or GitHub Apps; any local-override mechanism for simultaneous library and consumer edits.
- Committing `Cargo.lock` (it stays git-ignored unless the scratch proof shows release-plz needs it, which then goes to the owner).
- Major versions, `semver_check`, `!` commits and `BREAKING CHANGE:` footers (1.x policy).
- Whole suites, Aspire end-to-end cells, platform matrices, Playwright or CI runs to close the epic.

## What the source changed in the shared brief

1. `dotnet/RayX.SignalR.E2E.Tests/src/Contracts/WorkflowContractTests.cs` pins exactly three workflows and forbids, in every workflow, `push` triggers, `write` permissions, `secrets.` references, persisted checkout credentials, actions outside an allowlist, top-level concurrency without `cancel-in-progress: true` and the word `publish`. Adding `release-plz.yml` and the Quality push trigger without changing it breaks `quality / contracts`, so the epic edits the .NET contract and validates it with `dotnet test`, although the release workflow itself needs only Rust.
2. `quality.yml` and `e2e.yml` run on every pull request to `master` (`paths-ignore: .agentx/**` only); `perf.yml` is dispatch-only. A release PR changes `Cargo.toml`, so a paths filter cannot skip it without skipping real manifest changes: the guard keys on the release-plz head branch instead.
3. The repository's memory commits are mostly `docs(agentx)` (47 commits) rather than `chore(agentx)` (9): the changelog skips both. The history also holds 8 pre-1.0 `feat(client)!` commits; they precede `v1.0.0` and never reach a release PR.
4. There is no README "Install"/"Use" section: the README has `## Installation` with an untagged git dependency, and `docs/01-getting-started.md`, `docs/08-tls.md`, the skill's `SKILL.md`, `references/setup-and-connection.md` and `references/tls.md` carry untagged git and `path = "../RayX.SignalR"` snippets. All consumer snippets move to the tag form.
5. `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` (identical) and the skill say RayX depends on the crate by path; RayX actually uses the untagged git URL (its `Cargo.lock` holds `b261c98`, version 0.2.0). RayX.GameX does depend by path. `CLAUDE.md` also says `publish = false` "until a registry and release policy exist", which this epic answers.
6. The crate version feeds the User-Agent (`src/communication/headers.rs`: `RayX SignalR/1.0 (1.0.0; …)` after the bump); the existing unit test is version-agnostic.
7. There are no tags yet; 24 non-conventional commits in the history do not matter because v1.0.0 is tagged with a hand-written changelog section.
8. `Cargo.lock` is git-ignored; `cargo package --no-verify` works for this `publish = false` package (403 files, checked during planning).

## Assumptions

- release-plz's release PR branches start with `release-plz-` (its default; RayX.CLI's PRs #4, #6 and #8 used `release-plz-<timestamp>`), and `pr_branch_prefix` sets it explicitly.
- `release-plz/action@v0.5` installs release-plz itself and needs only `cargo` on the runner, as on RayX.CLI.
- release-plz reads the GitHub Release notes for v1.0.0 from the `## [1.0.0]` section of `CHANGELOG.md`; if not, FIRST-2 handles it.

## Risks

- Implementation is pushed straight to `master`, so the end-to-end suite runs only when `e2e.yml` is dispatched (or on a non-release pull request); Quality's light jobs run on every push to `master`, its full matrices only on pull requests. The first push is also Quality's first run on a `master` push: an unrelated red job (for example a new RustSec advisory in `dependency-security`) goes through the repair loop.
- A test-only fix committed as `fix(e2e)` opens a patch release PR; docs ask for `test`/`ci` types instead.
- A stray `!` or `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer makes release-plz propose `2.0.0`; the 1.x merge check catches it before the merge.
- `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` is the PAT created for "only RayX.CLI"; if its repository access was not extended to RayX.SignalR, the first Release-plz run fails at checkout or push. FIRST-2 then reports to the owner (fix: add the repository to the PAT) instead of retrying.
- A rebase that rewrites checkpointed commits invalidates AgentX checkpoints (see constraints).

## Owner prerequisites (done 2026-10-18; sprint s3 verifies them)

- `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` exists as a repository secret of RayX.SignalR (set 2026-10-18T21:08:30Z; the same PAT RayX.CLI uses).
- The tag ruleset `Release tags` (id 25358679: `refs/tags/v*`; rules `update`, `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`; no bypass; creation allowed) and the branch ruleset `DefaultProtection` (default branch; `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`; bypass for the owner's account, so the owner-credential `--force-with-lease` push works) exist.
- The owner pre-approved the first-release push and every release-PR merge of this epic. Other outward-facing repairs (editing Release notes, closing a stray release PR, the by-hand fallback tag) still need the owner's go-ahead.
- `global.json` pins .NET SDK `10.0.402` (commit `9687cce`, the epic's baseline on `master`); `dotnet --version` reports it and the E2E test project builds.
constraintsMarkdown:
## Owner decisions (2026-10-18), binding: do not re-open

1. Git tags, not crates.io. Manifests stay valid for packaging, but nothing is published to a registry: `publish = false` stays in `Cargo.toml` and in `release-plz.toml`.
2. Consumers pin `{ git = "https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.SignalR", tag = "vX.Y.Z" }`; `Cargo.lock` records the commit; a `v*` tag ruleset blocks moving and deleting tags.
3. Every library starts at **1.0.0**.
4. One shared fine-grained PAT as the Actions secret `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` (exists for this repository since 2026-10-18).
5. No local-override mechanism for simultaneous library and consumer edits: no documented `[patch]` file, no path-dependency instructions for consumers. A change spanning this library and RayX releases the library first; RayX bumps its tag by hand.
6. No Renovate, no Dependabot changes, no GitHub App.

## Amendment 1 (owner, 2026-10-18, later the same day), binding

- **Stay on 1.x.** No commit is marked breaking: no `!` after the type or scope, no `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. A breaking change is committed as `feat` (minor), or `fix` when it is a fix, and its body states the break. `semver_check = false`; `release_commits = "^(feat|fix|perf)"`. Before merging a release PR, check its proposed version is still `1.x`; a `2.0.0` proposal means a stray `!`/`BREAKING CHANGE:` commit, which is reworded (force push allowed) instead of merging. The policy ends when a second consumer appears; then `!` and major bumps return.
- **Light CI on `master`.** `quality.yml` also runs on pushes to `master` (its pull-request trigger stays); a push runs only rustfmt, clippy and the Rust unit tests on ubuntu, every other Quality job is skipped on push by a job-level `github.event_name != 'push'` clause; `e2e.yml` and `perf.yml` do not run on push; the `WorkflowContract` tests allow exactly that. Release PRs still skip the heavy jobs.
- **Migration footers.** A breaking change is a `feat` whose body states the break, with consumer notes in a `Migration:` footer; the changelog template renders those footers.
- **Prerequisites done.** The secret and the `Release tags` ruleset exist; sprint s3 verifies them and creates nothing.
- **Blanket go-ahead.** The first-release push and every release-PR merge are pre-approved; the checks stay (the light Quality jobs green where they run, the proposed version stays `1.x`, a release PR changes only `Cargo.toml` and `CHANGELOG.md`).
- **Baseline.** The epic starts from `9687cce` on `master` (`build(dotnet): pin the .NET SDK to 10.0.402`).

## Push / PR / validation policy (owner, 2026-10-18)

- Implement and test **locally** with focused checks only. This work needs no Aspire end-to-end cells, platform matrices, Playwright suites, performance runs or CI runs to close the epic.
- Push straight to `master` with a force push, always in the safe form: `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/master` first, then `git push --force-with-lease origin master`, so a push never drops a remote commit (a merged release PR, a commit a release tag points to). No feature branches and no pull requests for implementation work. The `DefaultProtection` branch ruleset lets the owner's credentials force-push.
- Pull requests are used ONLY for releases (release-plz's release PR). Merging one is outward-facing; the owner pre-approved the merges in this epic, subject to the checks above.
- In git-only mode the first release needs no PR: with `Cargo.toml` at `1.0.0` and no `v*` tag, release-plz's `release` job tags `v1.0.0` on the push to `master`. Therefore `release-plz.yml` lands in the same push as (or after) the `1.0.0` version, never before it.
- `CLAUDE.md`: Conventional Commits with meaningful scopes; never add Claude co-author lines.

## Epic constraints

- **One push.** No commit of this epic reaches `origin` before task `t09-first-release-push`; that push carries every commit (release workflow, version, changelog, docs, contracts and AgentX state). It cuts v1.0.0 because the secret exists; it is pre-approved.
- **Checkpoint SHAs.** AgentX checkpoints pin commit SHAs. Start from `9687cce`: run `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/master` before starting sprint s1; before the push, continue only if `origin/master` is an ancestor of `HEAD` (the rebase is then a no-op). If `master` moved, stop and ask the owner instead of rewriting checkpointed commits.
- Library source, Rust tests, benches, `build.rs`, toolchain pins, `perf.yml` and `LICENSE` stay unchanged (forbidden paths). The only manifest change is `version`.
- Repository rules hold: crates.io dependencies only and no new NuGet packages for these contracts (a new package would need the `DependencySecurity` scan); no scripts in the repository (`RepositoryTests` forbids `.sh`, `.ps1`, `.mjs`, `.cmd`, `.bat`); test workflows keep `contents: read`, no secrets, disabled credential persistence, failure-only redacted uploads and their check names; no workflow contains the word `publish`.
- The release workflow needs only Rust (never .NET). The repository's governance contracts are .NET xUnit facts and run locally with the .NET SDK `10.0.402` that `global.json` pins (installed).
- This epic's own commits use no `!` and no `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer (1.x policy).
- The implementer never prints, stores or commits the PAT. Raw output (scratch release-plz runs, `gh` output) goes to the ignored `artifacts-temp/agentx/signalr-releases/`.

requirements.title: release-plz releases by git tag
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Conventional Commits on `master` turn into release PRs, tags and GitHub Releases without a registry.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`release-plz.toml` at the repository root configures the single package for a git-only release:

- `[workspace]`: `git_only = true`, `publish = false`, `git_tag_enable = true`, `git_tag_name = "v{{ version }}"`, `git_release_enable = true` (release-plz creates the GitHub Release; there is no cargo-dist), `changelog_update = true`, `pr_branch_prefix = "release-plz-"`, `semver_check = false` with a comment above it naming the 1.x policy (an API break cargo-semver-checks found would force a major bump), and exactly `release_commits = "^(feat|fix|perf)"` with a comment that a breaking change is typed `feat` (or `fix`) and states the break in its body.
- The `release_commits` regex, as written in the file, matches `feat: x`, `feat(client): x`, `fix(client): x` and `perf(protocol): x`, and does not match `docs: x`, `docs(agentx): x`, `chore(agentx): x`, `chore(release): x`, `test(e2e): x`, `ci: x`, `build(test): x`, `refactor(quality): x`, `chore: release v1.0.1` or `Merge pull request #2 from rayx-ui/x`. (`!` and `BREAKING CHANGE:` are not used under the 1.x policy, so no sample carries them.)
- `[[package]] name = "rayx-signalr"` (CHANGELOG.md at the root, the default path).
- `[changelog]` is RayX.CLI's template: a `header` starting `# Changelog` that names `rayx-signalr`, links Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 and Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 and says it is generated from Conventional Commits by release-plz; a `body` whose heading is `## [{{ version }}] - {{ timestamp | date(format="%Y-%m-%d") }}` with groups, scopes and the `[**breaking**]` marker, and that renders every `Migration:` footer of a commit (git-cliff `commit.footers`, `footer.token == "Migration"`) as an indented `- Migration: <value>` line under that commit's line; `trim = true`, `protect_breaking_commits = true`, `tag_pattern = "v[0-9].*"`, `sort_commits = "oldest"`; `commit_parsers` that skip `^chore\(agentx\)`, `^docs\(agentx\)`, `^chore\(release\)` and `^chore\(deps\)` and group feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs, ci/build, test and chore as the CLI does.

Verified by the new group `Case=release-automation` (`dotnet/RayX.SignalR.E2E.Tests/src/Contracts/ReleaseAutomationTests.cs`), which asserts the keys and the `Migration` footer loop in the body and applies the regex extracted from the file to the sample messages; the rendering itself is proven by RPZ-2.

requirements.title: The release workflow and its governance
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: One push-triggered, Rust-only workflow runs release-plz; the repository's workflow contract governs it alongside the test workflows.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`WorkflowContractTests.cs` governs four workflows: `Workflows()` expects `e2e.yml`, `perf.yml`, `quality.yml` and `release-plz.yml`. Triggers follow RPR-2 (push only for `quality.yml` and `release-plz.yml`, only `master`). `release-plz.yml` is the only workflow that may declare `write` permissions (only the job-level grants of WF-1), reference a secret (only `secrets.RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN`), keep checkout credentials (its checkouts carry the PAT `token` instead of `persist-credentials: false`), use `release-plz/action@v0.5` besides `actions/checkout@v7`, and omit a top-level `cancel-in-progress: true` concurrency. Every other existing assertion still holds unchanged for `e2e.yml`, `quality.yml` and `perf.yml` (`contents: read`, no secrets, `persist-credentials: false`, the action allowlist, failure-only and performance uploads), and every workflow, `release-plz.yml` included, still forbids schedules, `publish`, `pull_request_target`, scripts and WebDriver tooling.

Verified by `dotnet test … --filter Category=WorkflowContract` (the existing facts and the new release workflow facts).

requirements.title: CI triggers: Quality on master pushes, no heavy suite on release pull requests
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Quality proves every push to `master`; a release PR changes only `Cargo.toml` and `CHANGELOG.md` (`Cargo.lock` is git-ignored), so it runs only the cheap format and lint gates.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`quality.yml` triggers on `pull_request` to `master` (unchanged, `paths-ignore: .agentx/**`) and on `push` to `master` with the same `paths-ignore: .agentx/**` (pushes that only change AgentX state run nothing). A push runs only the light jobs `quality / rustfmt`, `quality / clippy` and `quality / unit-contract (<protocol>)`, all on ubuntu; `native`, `wasm`, `android`, `ios`, `threaded-wasm`, `platform`, `rustdoc`, `dependency-security` and `contracts` carry the job-level

`if: ${{ github.event_name != 'push' && !(startsWith(github.head_ref, 'release-plz-') && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) }}`

(the push clause combined with RPR-1's release-PR clause), so they report skipped on a push and run as before on pull requests. `e2e.yml` keeps `pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch` and `perf.yml` keeps `workflow_dispatch` only; neither runs on `push`. The `WorkflowContract` tests allow exactly that: a `push` trigger only in `quality.yml` and `release-plz.yml`, each with `branches: [master]` and no other branch; in `quality.yml` every job except the light ones skips on push; `quality.yml` still requires `pull_request`; `e2e.yml` and `perf.yml` still forbid `push`. The top comments of `quality.yml` and `e2e.yml` say which events start which jobs. Quality's per-ref concurrency (`cancel-in-progress: true`) stays, so a newer `master` push supersedes an older run.

Verified by the new group `Case=release-automation` (trigger blocks per workflow, the push clause per Quality job by id) and `Category=WorkflowContract`.

Every job of `e2e.yml` except `soak` (already dispatch-only) and every job of `quality.yml` except `rustfmt` and `clippy` carries the release-PR clause in its job-level condition: alone on the `e2e.yml` jobs and `quality / unit-contract`,

`if: ${{ !(startsWith(github.head_ref, 'release-plz-') && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) }}`

and combined with RPR-2's push clause on the other Quality jobs. So on a release PR (a same-repository head branch starting `release-plz-`) only `quality / rustfmt` and `quality / clippy` run and every other job reports skipped. Ordinary pull requests, a fork branch that happens to start with `release-plz-`, pushes to `master` (including the merge of a release PR) and `workflow_dispatch` runs are unaffected. Job ids, names, matrices, commands and the existing `if:` of `soak` stay unchanged (stable check names; `master` has no required checks, so skipped jobs block nothing). The prefix in the condition equals `pr_branch_prefix` in `release-plz.toml`. `perf.yml` (dispatch only) is unchanged.

Verified by the new group `Case=release-automation` (each job's exact condition by id, and the prefix agreement) and by `Category=WorkflowContract` (all existing per-job assertions still hold).

requirements.title: Version 1.0.0 and the changelog
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: The crate starts its released life at 1.0.0 with a changelog release-plz continues.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown:
`Cargo.toml` says `version = "1.0.0"`; nothing else in the manifest changes (`publish = false`, `license = "MIT"`, both authors including the original signalr-client author, edition 2021, `rust-version = "1.92"`, features and dependencies). No other manifest requires the crate's version (`tests/wasm-fixture/Cargo.toml` uses a path without `version`). A new root `CHANGELOG.md` starts with exactly the `[changelog] header` text of `release-plz.toml` and has a `## [1.0.0] - YYYY-MM-DD` section.

As a lasting invariant the contract asserts that the manifest version (from `cargo metadata --no-deps`) is at least `1.0.0` and below `2.0.0` (the 1.x policy; the assertion's message says to change it together with `docs/releasing.md` when the policy ends) and that `CHANGELOG.md` has a `## [<that version>] - YYYY-MM-DD` heading, so later release PRs keep both in step. The existing unit test `request_headers_user_agent_follows_the_official_format` passes with the new version (User-Agent `RayX SignalR/1.0 (1.0.0; …)`).

Verified by the new group `Case=release-consumption` (`dotnet/RayX.SignalR.E2E.Tests/src/Contracts/ReleaseConsumptionTests.cs`) and `cargo test --lib request_headers_user_agent_follows_the_official_format`.

The `## [1.0.0] - <date>` section summarises what the first release offers, in the style of RayX.CLI's 1.0.0 section (one introductory sentence, then short grouped bullets), and fabricates no history (no earlier versions, invented dates or commit lists). It covers: every SignalR call style (`invoke`, `send`, server streams, server-to-client calls with client results); JSON and MessagePack (`messagepack`); retry policies and ASP.NET Core stateful reconnect; the .NET client's lifecycle (`new`/`start`/`stop`, hooks, `status()`, `pause`/`resume`, keep-alive and timeouts); WebSockets, Server-Sent Events and Long Polling with fallback; the targets (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android, iOS, browser `wasm32-unknown-unknown` on the main thread, in Web Workers and multithreaded; WASI unsupported); TLS options (`tls-platform-verifier` and `tls-ring` by default, `tls-webpki-roots`, `tls-aws-lc-rs`, client certificates, private CAs); proxies (system proxy by default, explicit HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS, `proxy-pac`); HTTP/2 and experimental HTTP/3 (`http3`); the typed `Error`/`ErrorKind`; MSRV 1.92; and that releases are git tags, not a registry. Every statement matches the README and `docs/`. The date is the day the version commit is pushed (task t09 re-dates it in a new commit if the push slips). Verified by review.

requirements.title: Consumption and release documentation
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: Consumers learn to pin a release tag; the owner and agents learn how releases happen.

requirements.title: The first release (GitHub-dependent)
requirements.descriptionMarkdown: v1.0.0 is tagged and released by release-plz on GitHub, and a consumer resolves it by tag.

criteria.descriptionMarkdown: Verify only (the owner created both on 2026-10-18; create nothing): `gh secret list --repo rayx-ui/RayX.SignalR` lists `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` (names only; the implementer never sees the value); `gh api repos/rayx-ui/RayX.SignalR/rulesets` and the detail of `Release tags` show an active tag ruleset including `refs/tags/v*` with the rules `update`, `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`, no bypass actors and no `creation` rule (release-plz may create tags); the active branch ruleset `DefaultProtection` on the default branch blocks deletion and non-fast-forward pushes with a bypass for the owner's account, so the owner-credential `--force-with-lease` push is allowed. A missing or different setting is reported to the owner, not changed. Verified by the recorded `gh` output.

A scratch Cargo project outside every repository (a fresh directory under the system temporary directory, with its own empty `[workspace]`) that depends on `rayx-signalr = { git = "https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.SignalR", tag = "v1.0.0" }` resolves it: `cargo generate-lockfile` succeeds and its `Cargo.lock` lists `rayx-signalr` with `version = "1.0.0"` and `source = "git+https://github.com/rayx-ui/RayX.SignalR?tag=v1.0.0#<sha>"`, where `<sha>` equals `git rev-parse v1.0.0^{commit}`; `cargo check` of a `lib.rs` that names `rayx_signalr::SignalRClient` with default features succeeds. Verified by the recorded command output.
